subject: Culture
title: Egyptian Mummification
description: A short lesson to help you apply Egyptian Mummification.

hook.text: The Egyptian embalming process took 70 days. The brain was pulled out through the nose with a hooked tool.

buildup.text: Egyptians believed the body was needed in the afterlife. Preservation was a passport to eternity.

discovery.text: Only elites got full mummification. Commoners were buried in desert sand—which often preserved them just as well.

twist.text: In the 1800s, Europeans ground up mummies for paint pigment called 'mummy brown' and for medicinal powders.

climax.text: CT scans now reveal diseases, diets, and injuries in mummies—3,000-year-old medical records preserved in linen.

punchline.text: They preserved their dead. Their dead preserved their history.

quiz.question: How long did Egyptian mummification take?
